Twenty-six. El Profe could be staring straight at him and he'd see nothing.

El Brody times it like a Corrida feint — the half-step slowdown masked inside the natural rhythm of the line shuffling forward. His shoulder dips a fraction as if adjusting his bag strap. His eyes find Valeria's for exactly one beat.

The wink is quick, easy, gone before it existed.

Valeria's pen stops mid-word on her clipboard. Her eyes flick down immediately — professional, composed — but the corner of her mouth twitches. One tiny muscle. She clears her throat, makes a mark on the clipboard that is almost certainly nonsense, and doesn't look up again until El Brody is three steps past and off the gangplank.

Nobody saw a thing. Hugol is still dissecting the Kaiserheim delegation with his eyes. El Profe is already moving down the gangplank behind the last of the team, clipboard tucked under his arm, calling out names for a headcount. The moment existed for exactly two people and then it was gone.

El Brody's boots hit the dock. The stone is warm through the soles — sun-baked and ancient, worn smooth by generations of fighters who walked this same stretch on their way to the Estádio do Sol. The crowd presses against the rope barriers on either side, a wall of faces and flags and noise. A cluster of fans in Carnivalia's crimson-and-violet are chanting something rhythmic and aggressive. A lone vendor is trying to sell miniature team flags to disembarking competitors — he holds up a La Selección pennant toward the group, hopeful, then quietly puts it back in the stack when nobody bites.

El Profe reaches the front and turns to face the team. Fourteen fighters, one medic, one coach. The full squad, standing on foreign stone.

"The Competitors' Village is up the Caminho do Sol. Twenty-minute walk. We stay together, we don't stop, we don't engage with crowds or press. Anyone who wanders off carries their own bags and finds their own lodge." His gaze sweeps the line. It passes over El Brody. Keeps going. "Move."

The team starts up the broad stone road that switchbacks up the coastal bluff. The Caminho do Sol stretches ahead — lined with vendors, buskers, and clusters of fans from nations El Brody has only ever heard about. Somewhere above, the Estádio do Sol waits on the clifftop.
